analyzed_vuln.description: `labelRecursivePatterns()` assumes every `')'` has a corresponding state entry. The state list starts with only `BASE`; on each closing parenthesis, lines 176-177 unconditionally call `state.back()` and `state.pop_back()` without checking whether the list contains a matching `BRANCH`/`RECURSE` entry. An unmatched first `')'` removes the `BASE` sentinel, and a subsequent `')'` operates on the empty `std::list`, causing undefined behavior and the observed invalid free in `pop_back()`. The function should reject unbalanced closing parentheses before accessing/popping the list (and should also validate recursive-pattern stack balance).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A parsed V2000 mol block reaches `ParseMolBlockProperties()` with an `M  MRV ...` Marvin SMARTS property line whose text has `SMA` at columns 7-9 and a valid in-range atom index. `ParseMarvinSmartsLine()` extracts everything from column 15 as attacker-controlled SMARTS and passes it to `SmartsToMol()`, which calls `labelRecursivePatterns()` before the SMARTS parser can reject malformed syntax. In this PoV the line `M  MRV6SMA   2  SBT3))))...` selects atom 2 and supplies SMARTS beginning ` SBT3))))...`; its excess closing parentheses exhaust the one-element state list and make the next close parenthesis trigger the bad free.
